items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: They want to see Desi Arnaz.

ctx.x: Well I’m glad you said that because I actually had a question for you and you are in a large sense a percussionist who came from Cuba. Has that resulted in people making assumptions about you? For instance, “Oh yeah, Ignacio, does he play the timbales or the congas or the bongos?” © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah it has been that way, especially with the people in the industry. My peers, my colleagues, those that know me from the days of the Dizzy Gillespie days, those who have followed my career, those who know my albums, my three albums, those who have seen me playing in jam sessions, they know, and I consider myself I’m a straight ahead jazz player. But what happens? It has nothing to do with being American, being Cuban, being from Senegal, Senegalese, or from Peru. It is human nature. And here in the United…

All right. Well you’ve been able to get out of the box on the projects you’ve done. And the one you sent me, “Straight Ahead from Havana,” when I listen to it I’m fascinated by the compositions for one thing, and how interactive the whole trio is with all the accents and the, it’s complex. And you’re right there with all of that. You’re very active on this record, and I’m not sure if I have a question here except that I admire it and it’s wonderful music.
